Issued at 200 PM EDT Fri Jul 31 2026

- Showers with isolated storms this evening into early Sunday

Upper trough close to closing off near the MN/IA border this 
afternoon remains poised to bring a period of rain beginning this 
evening, and continuing potentially into early Sunday. 

The better rain axis begins just west of the Chicago/Milwaukee areas 
early this afternoon. This will take some time and evolve as it 
moves toward the area. The system overall is a slow mover as it 
closes off aloft. In addition, we have a fair amount of dry air 
aloft that will eat away at the leading edge of the precipitation 
shield.

In addition, the nose of the 850 mb low level jet is driving a lot 
of this initial rain. The way the upper low is moving SE, the 
convergence ahead of the low level jet is not impressive over our 
area tonight as the better convergence moves south of the area. We 
expect rain amounts to be on the lighter side through most of 
tonight, but high probabilities moving through the night. 

Then on Saturday, we transition from the forcing via the low level 
jet, to more the deformation zone of the upper low and resulting mid 
level fgen Saturday morning and early afternoon. This actually looks 
to be the best potential for rain for most of the area during this 
entire event. 

The potential for thunder is rather low, but non-zero for tonight 
and Saturday morning. The better chance actually looks to be once 
the mid level deformation likely moves out, and we see the rain 
scatter out a bit, and some heating take place. The cold pool aloft 
combined with the diurnal warming will produce enough instability to 
pop some showers and isolated storms tomorrow afternoon and early 
evening. Some of these could be locally heavy with Precipitable 
Water values quite a bit elevated to around 2.0 inches. We are not
expecting event totals to cause any hydrology issues. We could be
looking at some local flood advisories with prolonged heavy
downpours over any one location.

The upper low remains close enough, with the occluded front lifting 
northward to SE LOwer then on Sunday. Much of the area should end up 
dry on Sunday with a dry flow coming in from the NNW to NNE. The SE 
corner of the forecast area is likely to keep some rain chances in 
most of Sunday. One thing we have to watch for as is typical with 
upper lows, is the exact movement of it. The models don't typically 
nail down the exact track with slight strength differences and short 
waves helping to complicate progs.

- Watching the upper low position for Monday and Tuesday

The best thought right now for Monday and Tuesday is that we should 
see drier conditions return to all of the area with seasonable 
temperatures. We see the large upper ridge over the Western U.S. be 
pushed toward the area by Monday and linger through Tuesday.

The caveat to this is dependent on the upper low being pushed out 
also. There is a chance that the upper low could be delayed in 
moving out. This could happen with the large ridge over the Atlantic 
holding up the progression of the low, and/or the upper low could 
remain closed and want to hold over the area a bit longer. We will 
ride the drier forecast for now, but this will have to be monitored.

- Another period of rain chances mid week

Also dependent on the upper low moving out, will be the next system 
that will be trying to move toward the area around mid-week next 
week. We see a stronger long wave trough that initially pushes the 
ridge toward the area. Then a piece of that trough continues east, 
and tries to flatten the ridge a bit. If it does not get blocked 
from coming in, it looks to affect the area late Tuesday into early 
Thursday. This pattern should keep the area from being affected 
strongly by any big heat ridge for now.
